items.summary: Physicists at CERN’s Large Hadron Collider have captured the clearest evidence yet that quark-gluon plasma, the scorching-hot matter that filled the newborn universe, behaves like a true liquid. items.title: As the planet warms, cities like Bangkok could be increasingly inundated by deadly floods
items.summary: In the humid tropics of Southeast Asia, afternoon thunderstorms roll through almost every day. Daytime heat causes towering, fluffy cumulonimbus clouds to form and swell before unleashing torrential rain on cities such as Singapore, Hong Kong and Bangkok. items.title: Yosemite's meadows can be restored, but it will take time and effort
items.summary: Researchers at Colorado State University are leading an attempt to restore Yosemite National Park's iconic meadows before it's too late by reintroducing native plants that once covered the landscape. Results are published in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Biogeosciences.

items.title: Rising heat linked to faster telomere loss in wild Australian birds
items.summary: Extreme heat can have a profound impact on wild animals, causing their death in the most extreme cases and leaving less visible marks in others. items.title: Seagrass meadows bounce back with new fish communities
items.summary: Seagrasses are flowering plants that thrive in marine environments and form extensive meadows along the tropical Queensland coast. items.summary: New mothers paired with patient navigators were much more likely to receive postpartum care, depression screening, preventive testing, and ongoing primary care. items.title: Cancer survival is improving, but return‑to‑work support is falling behind
items.summary: Australia has made significant strides in improving cancer survival, but new research from Griffith University finds far less progress in supporting survivors' return to work, which remains a major challenge for many. items.title: New report reveals gaps in corporate modern slavery disclosures
items.summary: Many of Australia's largest companies fail to show enough public evidence that workers affected by modern slavery can safely report concerns, a new Monash University–led report has found.

items.title: Francis Halzen wins Nobel Prize in physics for work on mysterious ghost particles called neutrinos
items.summary: Francis Halzen won the Nobel Prize in physics on Tuesday for his efforts to demystify a rare group of neutrinos, tiny cosmic particles that scientists believe offer clues to how the universe evolved.

items.title: Nature's capacity to 'bounce back' when species are lost is vastly overestimated, global analysis finds
items.summary: The idea that ecosystems carry plenty of backup, so if a small number of species become extinct there is little harm, has been greatly overestimated, according to the largest global study of its kind.

items.title: Scientists finally see how nature moves energy so efficiently
items.summary: Researchers have captured key steps in a chemical reaction that helps nature transfer energy with remarkable efficiency. items.title: California scientist wins a Nobel Prize, then makes school lunches for his kids
items.summary: Dr. Karl Deisseroth spent hours fielding congratulatory calls after learning early Monday that he had won a Nobel Prize for medicine for helping to open a new field of brain science called optogenetics.

items.title: Switching on brain cells: The Nobel-winning science of optogenetics
items.summary: In optogenetics, scientists control neurons by stimulating them with light—potentially unlocking breakthroughs for conditions such as dementia, depression and blindness.

items.title: Russia reports a worker at a Siberian plague institute got pneumonia from an unknown cause and died
items.summary: Russian authorities have quarantined a hospital and are monitoring contacts of an employee at a plague research institute in Siberia who contracted pneumonia of an "unknown" cause. Local state TV said the woman died last week.
